t: How Read-Aloud Can Improve Behavior And Instill A Lifelong Love Of Reading
q: Sadly, in recent years, much of the joy of read-aloud has been sucked out and driven away by over-instruction.
We turn works of art into just another academic exercise, destroying the very qualities that draw students into a love of reading.
Once you begin a read-aloud, don’t stop until you run out of time. Don’t stop to analyze the text, explain vocabulary, ask questions, or take breaks for students to discuss.
Honor the story and author and read them from start to finish and as they were intended.
It’s your one guaranteed academic success connection with every student, no matter how much they may be struggling.
Find time for read-aloud every day. Defend it as your one sacred non-negotiable.

t: How Today's Students Are Different And What It Means For You
q: Students today are more appreciative, more influenced, and more affected by teachers who are consistently kind and pleasant.
Simple, day-after-day kindness is the one sure way to gain leverage and influence with any group of students, no matter how challenging.
Today’s students are savvy and worldly and have a deep conviction that negative methods of classroom management are not okay with them.
The hard truth is that there is no longer a place for lecturing, scolding, glaring, and the like in an effective teacher’s toolkit.
